$comment: DG-6201 standby diesel generator set twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from the Cummins data sheet, NFPA 110, ISO 8528-5 and commissioning data; the controller, the ATS and the tank gauges send only what they measure.

identification.model: C2000 D5 (50 Hz, 2063 kVA / 1650 kW standby, QSK60-G3 engine, PI734F alternator)
identification.description: Data centre standby generator set 1 of the emergency power supply system: 1650 kW standby at 400 V, 50 Hz
identification.site: Demo data centre, generator yard, set 1
identification.engine: Cummins QSK60-G3: cast iron 60 deg V16, turbocharged and low temperature after-cooled, 60 L, 1500 rpm, electronic governor
identification.alternator: STAMFORD PI734F, 380-440 V, brushless, with automatic voltage regulator (AVR)
identification.cooling: Set-mounted radiator for 40 C ambient, jacket water heater for standby
identification.fuel: Day tank on the set, filled by a transfer pump from the bulk tank
identification.starting: 24 V DC electric start, lead-acid starting batteries with a float charger
identification.transfer: Automatic transfer switch (ATS) between the utility and the set; it times every transfer
identification.monitoring: Generator set controller (Modbus), ATS controller, tank gauges, fuel water sensor

rating.source: Cummins data sheet C2000 D5 DS48-CPGK (05/19): standby 2063 kVA (1650 kW), prime 1875 kVA (1500 kW), 1500 rpm; Emergency Standby Power (ESP) and Prime Power (PRP) in accordance with ISO 8528. 400 V within the PI734F 380-440 V range.

engine.source: Cummins data sheet DS48-CPGK: QSK60-G3 cast iron 60 deg V16, bore 159 mm, stroke 190 mm, lube oil 378 L, coolant 456 L with radiator, electronic governor, 24 V DC starting, radiator ambient design 40 C, total heat rejection 48925 Btu/min at standby.

fuel.source: Cummins data sheet DS48-CPGK, standby fuel consumption 122 / 208 / 300 / 406 L/h at 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and full load. Curve a + b P + c P^2 fitted to these four points by build_twin.py. Diesel density 0.84 kg/L: assumption: typical value, replace with the fuel supplier's certificate.

exhaust.source: Exhaust gas temperature 440 C at the standby rating: Cummins data sheet DS48-CPGK. The straight line 140 C + 300 C x load fraction through that point and the +1 K per K of ambient: assumption: typical value, replace with the engine performance data and the load-bank test log of your set.

coolant.source: Coolant held at the thermostat while the radiator has spare capacity; above it the coolant settles at ambient + rise, the rise growing with the heat to reject (30 % of the full-load heat at no load). Radiator sized for 40 C ambient at full load (data sheet); thermostat 85 C, full-load rise 55 K and jacket water heater set point 40 C: assumption: typical value, replace with the engine and heater data.

start.source: NFPA 110 Type 10: power back at the transfer switch load terminals within 10 s. The split 1 s detection / 8.5 s start to ready-to-load / 0.5 s transfer is the one a Cummins PowerHour course on NFPA 110 uses. Lowest cranking voltage of a healthy 24 V battery and the largest load step the site applies: assumption: typical value, replace with the battery and starter data and the site's load-step plan.

transient.source: ISO 8528-5 performance class G3, diesel: transient frequency dip <= 7 %, recovery <= 3 s; voltage dip <= 15 %, recovery <= 4 s (Kohler / Rehlko white paper, from Table 4 of ISO 8528-5:2022). Class G3 as the site requirement: assumption: typical value, replace with the site specification.

tanks.source: Day tank 1000 L, bulk tank 25000 L, required run time at the standby rating 48 h and the data centre load the set carries in an outage 1200 kW: assumption: typical value, replace with the site's design basis (NFPA 110 calls the run time at rated load without refuelling the Class).

duty.source: NFPA 110 8.4.2: monthly exercise for at least 30 minutes at not less than 30 % of the standby nameplate kW, or at the manufacturer's minimum exhaust gas temperature; 8.3.7: fuel quality test at least annually.

demo.note: Demo only: the set runs a monthly test every two minutes or so of real time (ATS test transfer, start, 90 s on load, cool-down, stop). Counters such as light-load hours and fuel test age come from the failure modes, not from the demo clock.

groups.Engine: Engine state, speed, fuel and coolant
groups.Start: Last start (held until the next one)

Frequency dip at the last load step

twin_model.limits_source: Type 10 (10 s), the 8.5 s start budget, the 30 % test load and the G3 transient limits: NFPA 110, the Cummins course and ISO 8528-5 (see design). Every other limit is an assumption: fuel ratio, exhaust residual and spread, coolant residual, pre-start coolant, ATS time, minimum test exhaust temperature (the twin's own curve at 30 % load), light-load hours, water in fuel and day tank level. Replace them with the maker's and the site's values.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

starting_battery_weak.name: Starting battery weak (sulphation, a failed cell)
starting_battery_weak.symptoms: deep voltage dip while cranking, slow start, power back later than 10 s

jacket_heater_failure.name: Jacket water heater failed
jacket_heater_failure.symptoms: engine cold at the start: coolant near ambient

ats_slow.name: Transfer switch slow (mechanism, timer setting)
ats_slow.symptoms: set ready on time, load transferred late

injector_fault.name: Injector fault on one cylinder
injector_fault.symptoms: one cylinder exhaust port much colder than the others

air_restriction.name: Air filter restriction or turbocharger fouling
air_restriction.symptoms: both banks hotter than the curve, more fuel per kW, deeper frequency dip on a load step

radiator_fouling.name: Radiator fouled (dust, oil mist, blocked core)
radiator_fouling.symptoms: coolant above what the load and the ambient explain

light_load_testing.name: Monthly tests at light load (wet stacking)
light_load_testing.symptoms: test below 30 % load with cold exhaust, light-load hours pile up

fuel_water.name: Water in the fuel
fuel_water.symptoms: fuel water sensor rising in the day tank
